Comparing the Huna and Arab invasions: 30907 is the concept that sets the Hunas up as the first of the two encounters from outside, so the comparison belongs to it rather than to 30908/30909, which are the Arab half alone.
Harsha's Prayaga assembly and his giving away of wealth; 30889 is this set's Harsha concept. No concept covers the assembly itself.

Matches dynasties to capitals, three of the five being the Palas, Gurjara-Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas named in 30894. It also touches 30891 (Kanyakubja) and 30902 (Chola, Pallava), but the contending-dynasties concept carries most of it.

Pala prosperity from land-based markets and maritime trade: 30894 is the only concept naming the Palas. The economic concepts here (30903-30906) are about land grants and irrigation, not Pala commerce.
Krishna I and the Ellora Kailashanatha: the Rashtrakutas are named only in 30894, and this chapter's set has no art-and-architecture concept outside the Chalukya capitals (30900).
Kalhana and the Rajatarangini are exactly 30897's 'own historical record' for Kashmir.
'Monolithic' is architectural vocabulary for rock-cut work, and 30900 is the concept describing the cave and rock temples of Badami and Aihole. The set has no general architecture concept.
Abhinavagupta and Kashmir Shaivism belong to 30897, where Kashmir is given its own line of rulers and its own intellectual record.
Huna descendants assimilating into Indian society - 30907, the Huna concept.
'Mlechchha' is glossed where the chapter deals with peoples from outside, which 30907 opens (it is also the concept carrying the 'connected to the wider world' framing).
A guild sponsoring an irrigation tank is 30906, where small-scale irrigation works are treated as economic history.
Naming the 600-1200 CE span (Early Medieval) is the chapter's framing of five centuries as renewal, 30888.
Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita, the source for Harsha, so it belongs to the Harsha concept 30889. 30901 is the Chalukya court poet Ravikirti, a different court.
Gopala chosen in 750 CE in Bengal - the Palas 'from the east' in 30894.
Vikramashila founded by the Pala ruler Dharmapala - 30894, the only Pala concept; the set has no concept for the monastic universities.
Nagabhata I founding the Gurjara-Pratiharas - 30894.
Al-Masudi on a Rashtrakuta ruler's armies and his protection of mosques - the Rashtrakutas of 30894.
Sulaiman on a Gurjara-Pratihara ruler's cavalry and his hostility to the Arabs: the subject is that dynasty's strength, 30894, with the Arab encounter as context.
Narasimhavarman I's titles and campaigns: 30902 is the concept that takes the southern kingdoms in their own right. The set has no Pallava-specific concept.
The Pandyas at Madurai and their Tamil Mahabharata - the southern kingdoms concept, 30902.
Vijayalaya founding the revived Chola line - 30902.
Indian rulers resisting the Arab armies follows directly from 30909, the Sindh campaign under Muhammad bin Qasim.
The change in Arab religious policy in Sindh - 30909, the Sindh concept.
Indian mathematics and astronomy reaching Europe through Arab translators: 30908 is the concept of contact with the new Arab world from 637, the only home for that exchange.
Queen Didda is part of Kashmir's own line of rulers, 30897.
Bilingual inscriptions with the operative land-grant details in the local language: the land-grant system of 30903, which is what those records are for.
Chola prosperity through administration, navy and Kaveri irrigation - the southern kingdoms in their own right, 30902 (30906 is irrigation as a general economic fact).
The Aulikaras are significant here precisely for defeating the Hunas - 30907.
Why 600-1200 CE matters, answered as renewal and resilience - 30888's framing.
